sections.title: Choroidal Nevus vs. Melanoma: Clinical Features

rows: Oval, circular brown to slate grey lesion
Overlying drusen are typical; Depigmented halo is very common
Overlying orange pigment lipofuscin; Absence of drusen and halos; Presence of subretinal fluid
Sentinel vessels, choroidal folds, inflammation, rubeosis iridis, secondary glaucoma, Cataract

sections.title: Suspicious Nevus: Review & Referral Protocol
content: No suspicious features: Review at 6m until stability established, then annual review.
One or more suspicious features: Review every 4-6m.
≥ 3 suspicious features: Prompt referral for ocular oncology subspecialist assessment.

sections.title: Clinical Pearl: Mnemonic for Melanoma Risk

content.explanation: To Find Small Ocular Melanoma Using Helpful Hints Daily: T (Thickness >2mm), F (Fluid), S (Symptoms), O (Orange Pigment), M (Margin near Disc), UH (Ultrasonic Hollowness), HD (Halo absent/Drusen absent).

sections.title: Investigations for Choroidal Melanoma
content: Photographic documentation: Essential for serial monitoring.
FAF (Fundus Autofluorescence): Nevus = patchy increase. Melanoma = intense or diffuse increase.
OCT: Measures lesion thickness and detects subretinal fluid.

U/S (B-scan): Localized flat or slightly elevated lesion with internal homogeneity, low to medium reflectivity. Measures dimensions, detects extraocular extension, choroidal excavation, orbital shadowing. 'Collar stud' configuration is pathognomonic.
FA (Fluorescein Angiography): Shows intrinsic tumour 'dual circulation', mottled fluorescence (AV phase), late diffuse leakage and staining.
ICGA: Hypofluorescence throughout the study.
MRI: To demonstrate extraocular extension.
Biopsy & Immunocytochemistry: PAX8 expression helps differentiate. Melanoma and melanocytoma are PAX8 negative; pigmented adenocarcinoma is PAX8 positive.
Genetic Analysis: Loss of chromosome 3 (M3) and changes in chromosome 8 (8q) correlate with poor prognosis.
Systemic Investigation: Liver function tests, U/S, and chest radiography to detect metastatic spread.

rows: Prominent vortex vein ampulla (disappears with pressure)

sections.title: Melanoma: Prognosis & Treatment Options
content: Adverse Features: Large no. of epithelioid cells, mitotic activity, large dimensions, somatic BAP1 mutation (50% risk of metastasis), extrascleral extension, anterior location.
Brachytherapy: Tumour <20mm basal diameter, up to 10mm thick, vision salvage possible.
External Beam Radiotherapy: For large/posterior tumours unsuitable for brachy.
Stereotactic Radiotherapy: Targeted radiation.
Transpupillary Thermotherapy (TTT): Small tumours or adjunct to radiotherapy.
Transscleral Choroidectomy: Tumour <16mm diameter but too thick for radiation.
Light activation AU-011: Small melanomas (2-3.4mm).
Enucleation Criteria: Large size, optic disc invasion, extensive ciliary body/angle involvement, irreversible loss of vision, or poor patient motivation.

branches: Heritable (40%): Bilateral, Multifocal, predisposes to Trilateral RB (Pinealoblastoma), Osteosarcoma, Melanoma.
Non-heritable (60%): Unilateral, Non-transmissible, No 2nd cancer risk.
Inheritance: AD; 40% of offspring affected. 90% of unilateral are non-hereditary.
Sibling Risk: 1% if non-heritable. Screening via prenatal U/S and ophthalmoscopy until age 5-7.

rows: < 3mm small intraretinal tumour away from optic disc and fovea
> 3mm macular or juxtapapillary location with subretinal fluid
Tumour with focal subretinal or vitreous seeding within 3mm from tumour
Tumour with diffuse subretinal or vitreous seeding > 3mm from tumour
Extensive RB (>50% globe), NVG, haemorrhage, extension to optic nerve or AC

sections.title: Retinoblastoma: Management & Treatment
content: EUA Items: Hand/Face exam, Tonometry, Corneal diameter, AC exam, Ophthalmoscopy, Cycloplegic refraction.
Chemotherapy: IV (Carboplatin, Etoposide, Vincristine - 6 cycles), Intra-arterial (Group D), Intravitreal Melphalan (Vitreous seeding).
Local Therapy: TTT, Cryotherapy (triple freeze-thaw for pre-equatorial), Brachytherapy (anterior, no seeding).
Radiotherapy: EBRT reserved for residual/relapsed cases due to risk of 2nd cancers.
Enucleation (+10mm Optic Nerve): Used for Group E, NVG, AC infiltration, or optic nerve invasion.
Extraocular Extension: Adjuvant chemo (6m CEV) for massive retrolaminar spread; EBRT if cut end of nerve/sclera is involved.
Systemic Spread: Aggressive high-dose chemo and autologous stem cell rescue for CNS involvement.

sections.title: Red Flags: RB Differentials & CAR/MAR
content: RB Differentials: PFV (Anterior/Posterior), Coats Disease, ROP, Toxocariasis, Uveitis, Vitreoretinal Dysplasia, Retinoma, Astrocytoma.
Cancer Associated Retinopathy (CAR): Bronchial CA; Attenuated arterioles, disc pallor, abnormal ERG (photopic/scotopic).
Melanoma Associated Retinopathy (MAR): Cutaneous melanoma; Vitiligo; Bipolar cells are target; Good prognosis.

sections.title: Tuberous Sclerosis (Bourneville Disease)
content: Genetics: AD (40%), Sporadic (60%).
Classic Triad: Epilepsy, Mental retardation, Adenoma sebaceum.
Skin: Ash leaf spots, Shagreen patches, Subungual hamartomas, Skin tags, Café au lait spots.
Neuro: Intracranial subependymal nodules, Giant cell astrocytic hamartomas, Seizures.
Visceral: Renal angiomyolipoma/cysts, Cardiac rhabdomyomas, Pulmonary lymphangiomatosis.
Ocular: Astrocytoma, Patchy iris hypopigmentation, Atypical iris colobomas.

sections.title: Von Hippel-Lindau (VHL) Disease & Screening
content: Genetics: AD (VHL gene Chromosome 3); 20% sporadic.
Features: Retinal haemangioblastoma, Phaeochromocytoma, Renal carcinoma, Visceral cysts (kidney, liver, etc.), Polycythaemia, Endolymphatic sac tumours (inner ear).
Screening (Retinal): Annual from age 2-5; 6-monthly from 10-30y.
Screening (Systemic): Renal U/S (from 15y), 24h Urine VMA/Catecholamines (age 2-5y for Pheo), 2-yearly Abdominal/Brain MRI (from 15y).
Genetic testing for all 1st and 2nd degree relatives.

rows: Anterior uveitis, vitritis, multifocal chorioretinitis-like lesions
Conjunctival involvement, orbital involvement, Mikulicz syndrome, uveal infiltration
Vitritis (cells/flare/KPs), Multifocal retinal infiltrates, Coalescence of sub-RPE deposits ('leopard skin'), absence of CMO

sections.title: Toxicology: Ocular Side Effects of Drugs

rows: Corneal verticillata, Optic neuropathy, Anterior subcapsular deposits
Bulls-eye maculopathy, paracentral scotoma, vortex keratopathy
Yellowish-brown granules in endothelium/lens capsule, Retinopathy
Greyish-brown granular deposition in Descemet membrane, conjunctivitis
PSC cataract, then ASC cataract; secondary glaucoma
Uveitis, ciliary effusion, myopia, Stevens-Johnson Syndrome
Salt and pepper pigmentary disturbance, focal RPE loss
Decreased VA, photopsia, Xanthopsia/Cyanopsia/Chloropsia, reduced B-wave amplitude

sections.title: Associated Syndromes: CHRPE & Others
content: Familial Adenomatous Polyposis (FAP): Associated with CHRPE.
Gardner Syndrome: FAP + Osteomas (skull/mandible), soft tissue tumours (epidermoid cysts, lipoma).
Turcot Syndrome: FAP + CNS Tumours (medulloblastoma, glioma).
Investigation for Lymphoma: OCT (confirm absence of CMO), FA (granular blockage due to sub-RPE cells), U/S (vitreous debris, RD), Cytology (vitreous/subretinal), MRI with Gadolinium, Lumbar Puncture.
